# DSH Desktop · HarmonyOS Edition
> The **official DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web UI, unmodified**, running on HarmonyOS 2in1 / tablet ins
ide the system **ArkWeb** — with the dsh Host on a **real Node.js runtime embedded in the same proce
ss**. No Electron, no bundled Chromium, no ArkUI rewrite.
## What you get
- **The same dsh you already know** — sessions, tools, plugins, settings, themes. The frontend is up

stream, untouched; the agent host runs locally, so there is no relay, no CORS, no account gate.
- **
Nothing to render with** — the system WebView draws the UI, so the package ships only the agent runt

ime (≈42 MB payload) instead of a browser engine. The HAP is ≈88 MB.
- **Installs without restricted
permissions** — the default build is JIT-free (`compat`), so side-loading needs no ACL-bound permis

sion. A `jit` variant exists for devices granted the writable-code-memory permission.
- **Zero upstr
eam changes** — HarmonyOS differences live in an `ohos` profile, one bundle layer, seam plugins and

six audited shims. Upgrading dsh means re-running the pipeline, not re-doing patches.
- **Branded as
this product** — own icon, name and window title; the upstream preview notice and the DeepSeek firs
t-run dialog no longer open by themselves (both remain reachable in Settings).
## Two HarmonyOS editions
HarmonyOS gets **two independent editions** with the same shell architecture, the same unmodified We
b UI and the same data plane; the difference is **which runtime provides Node**:
| | **HarmonyOS Edition** (this repo) | **Electron on HarmonyOS Edition** (`dsh-desktop-hos`) |

| Renderer | The system **ArkWeb** — nothing bundled | Chromium, shipped inside Electron 37 |
| Node
.js | `libnode.so` started in the app's own process (v26.13.0) | Inside the Electron runtime (Node 2

2.17) |
| Runtime plumbing | `@fellow99/node-bridge` + `@fellow99/node-runtime` (ohpm) | `harmonypc-

electron` |
| Upstream dsh patches | **0** — profile + bundle layer + audited shims | 13 source patc

hes |
| Install requirement | none (JIT-free default) | JIT restricted permission (ACL) |
| Package

size | ≈88 MB | Electron-sized (hundreds of MB) |
| Maturity | 0.2.2 — built (0.2.1 device-verified
on HarmonyOS 6.1.0.135 / API 24) | 0.2.2 — built & signed (on-device re-verification pending; 0.2.0
S 6.1.0.135 / API 24) | 0.2.2 — built & signed (on-device re-verification pending; 0.2.0 baseline) |
Neither replaces the other: the Electron edition buys maximum desktop fidelity at the cost of a bund
led Chromium and JIT; this edition buys a small payload and a permission-free install at the cost of
covering platform gaps in the shim layer.
## Capabilities at a glance
| Area | State |

| dsh Web UI, sessions, tools, skills, subagents | ✅ works as upstream |
| File read / write / edit,

image attachments | ✅ |
| Workspace picker with Documents & Downloads (grant → read/write) | ✅ |
|

Git (21 tools, pure JS, no `git` binary needed) | ✅ |
| Local plugins loaded from the profile, own b

randing | ✅ |
| Command execution (`bash`) | ⚠️ executor ships; a path-resolution fix is pending |
|

Content search (`grep` / `glob`) | ⚠️ needs a pure-JS backend (no `ripgrep` binary on arm64) |
| De

lete / move / copy / chmod | ⚠️ upstream `ctx.fs` has no such primitives yet |
| Plugin marketplace,
tray icon, window-state memory | — not in this edition |
The complete matrix — every capability, both editions side by side, with root causes — is `docs/鸿蒙环境
trix — every capability, both editions side by side, with root causes — is `docs/鸿蒙环境能力清单-0.2.1.md`.
## Status
`0.2.2` (`versionCode` 202) — **built** for dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1 on Node 26.13.0 (on-device verification
pending; 0.2.1 device-verified on HarmonyOS 6.1.0.135 / API 24, 2in1): installs with zero ACLs, the
payload self-extracts and reports `ready`, all shims install, `node:sqlite`/FTS5 available, text and
image conversations, workspace picker across the three roots, git clone (public and intranet), and
the branded window (checked through the WebView debugger). Known gaps and their fix points are liste
d in the capability inventory above.
## Build
Prerequisites: DevEco **Command Line Tools** (SDK API 24) and the sibling submodule `../deepseek-har
ness`. The Node runtime is pulled from the OpenHarmony ohpm central repository: `@fellow99/node-brid
ge` (API + NAPI bootstrap) and `@fellow99/node-runtime@26.13.0` (the `libnode.so` engine, SHA-256-lo
cked by the bundled `runtime.lock.json`).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[该节后续省略]
### Signing (read this before wondering why a signed HAP fails)
`assembleHap` runs `hap-sign-tool.jar` via **whatever `java` is first on `PATH`** — the hvigor task
does not pin a JDK. If the machine also has another JDK (sdkman/Temurin, Adoptium, …), signing dies
with a misleading error that has nothing to do with the HAP:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`scripts/build-hap.sh` therefore prepends DevEco's bundled **JBR** (with `cygpath -u`, otherwise MSY
S bash cannot resolve `java.exe`) and exports `JAVA_HOME`. If you invoke `hvigorw` yourself, do the
same or you will hit that error.
Signing material is **never committed**. Either let DevEco Studio generate it (it writes `app.signin
gConfigs` into `build-profile.json5` — do not commit that file; revert it after building), or provid
e `signing.debug.local.json` / `signing.release.local.json` (gitignored) with **plaintext** password
s (`certpath`, `storeFile`, `profile`, `keyAlias`, `keyPassword`, `storePassword`, `signAlg`) — DevE
co's encrypted password strings only decrypt on the inline `build-profile.json5` path.
Run `bash scripts/build-hap.sh --debug` to get `entry-default-signed.hap`, which installs on a devic
e whose debug profile matches (`hdc app install -r …`). `--release` needs a release profile and can
only ship through AppGallery.
